answer: Each agent identity must lock a refundable bond, and a random pulse periodically asks it to prove control of a unique key. Every extra sybil the attacker mints needs its own bond, so cost rises linearly with the number of fakes; any caught clone forfeits its stake, slashed into permanent basalt. Honest agents later reclaim their relic. Flooding therefore costs real capital per fake identity, making Sybil swarms uneconomic.
